GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The predecessor's red hosted Source run is a visible symptom, but the repository inspection found a wider evidence mismatch: the claimed production CEF/native path is reference-backed, S3B bypasses the normal provider boundary, and artifact bytes live behind a downloads-local in-memory store. Treating the work as a lint-only repair would therefore create green source evidence without establishing the security, persistence and production-path claims needed for M1.3.
The remediation is intentionally a new bundle rather than an edit to the archived predecessor. That preserves the historical record of the prior applied state while allowing the new implementation and fresh evidence to state exactly what is repaired.

Alternatives.Alternative: Repair only the current clippy findings and rerun Source. This is not selected because it leaves the reference-backed provider, simulated S3B engine evidence, artifact authority gap and cookie-domain flaw intact.
Rewrite the archived predecessor as though its hosted evidence had passed. This is not selected because it would erase the audit trail and violate the GRACE apply lifecycle.

Retain a browser-downloads-specific artifact store and add a local authorization check. This is not selected because it duplicates a kernel concern and cannot demonstrate the established generic blob authority boundary.

Remove CEF from the proving claim and retain only deterministic reference fixtures. This is not selected because the M1.3 claim under remediation is specifically about the production native provider path.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: T-001 is an explicit feasibility gate, not an assumption that the existing simulated adapter is a binding. It must choose a pinned CEF distribution, executable C API binding, callback/refcount ownership, thread model, subprocess dispatch and true headful lifecycle before the provider can be treated as production-capable.
The plan will identify the smallest generic completion seam for brokered blob read admission and persisted download metadata without creating a browser-specific kernel facility.

The plan will determine whether the experimental 0.1 cookie and blob contracts can express the required semantics. If not, it will specify an additive experimental 0.2 or separately named experimental contract while retaining 0.1 fixtures and compatibility coverage.
The plan will select an RFC-aligned host canonicalization implementation and document its treatment of IDNA, trailing dots, IP literals and public suffix restrictions where those cases are in scope.

The local active/archive predecessor collision and unrelated incomplete downloads edits were isolated recoverably before the remediation plan was regenerated from a green GRACE baseline. The archived predecessor remains untouched historical evidence; recovery is not an implementation task in this plan.
The exact hosted Windows job names, runner fixtures and evidence links are implementation-plan and CI configuration details, not new normative requirements.

The provider implementation must re-prove the existing M1.2 safety claims against actual CEF: sandbox posture, authority-free child processes, process-tree containment, pinned DLL loading, privileged scheme rejection, and a true headful S2 path. A simulated loop or reference fallback cannot discharge that evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: A native provider started with --backend cef either reports a genuine CEF-backed capability surface or fails visibly; it never silently runs the reference backend.
A separately labelled reference test starts --backend reference and keeps deterministic fixtures available without being presented as production proof.

A loopback download reaches the downloads service through the normal provider and IPC path. A principal may inspect metadata with the downloads grant yet is denied bytes until it also receives generic blob-read authority; after restart the record remains resolvable.
Cookie operations distinguish example.com, sub.example.com and evil-example.com after canonicalization, preserve host-only scope and retain BrowserContextId isolation.

The remediation reaches local and hosted evidence while remaining neither applied nor archived as successfully applied until the required hosted result is green and an owner explicitly confirms apply.
